configuration: The single case of examples/kinematics-derivatives.cpp: computeForwardKinematicsDerivatives followed by two calls to getJointAccelerationDerivatives (LOCAL, then WORLD) for the end-effector joint (the last joint of the chain), on the same frozen fixed-base UR5 manipulator (6 revolute joints, nq=nv=6) and frozen configuration the sibling exc-* checks use, read from ic/<ic>/model.json and ic/<ic>/operands.json, with the joint velocity and the joint acceleration held at zero, exactly as the example sets them. Upstream reuses one set of four output buffers for both frame calls (the second overwrites the first); this adapter keeps a second set so both the LOCAL and the WORLD results are graded, instead of the example's own behaviour of discarding the LOCAL result. The model was produced once by a URDF-enabled scratch build of this leaf's own pinned source parsing models/example-robot-data/robots/ur_description/urdf/ur5_robot.urdf and frozen through the same model_io.hpp writer the checks load with; this leaf's own image builds Pinocchio with BUILD_WITH_URDF_SUPPORT=OFF, so no URDF parser runs in the check itself. See comment/README.md, 'Freezing the UR5', for the exact commands.
observable: the four blocks getJointAccelerationDerivatives fills for the end-effector joint (v_partial_dq, a_partial_dq, a_partial_dv, a_partial_da), in the LOCAL and in the WORLD frame, eight arrays in total
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that the model is read from ic/ instead of parsed from ur5_robot.urdf with pinocchio::urdf::buildModel, the configuration is a frozen draw instead of a fresh randomConfiguration() draw, and both frame results are kept in separate buffers instead of the second overwriting the first
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on five active initial-condition numbers: two operands of the frozen configuration, q[0] and q[3], and three model numbers, because the model is itself an initial-condition input and some graded quantities depend on it alone: the mass and the first lever component of the first body (shoulder_pan_joint) and the leading rotation entry of its placement (identity here; the UR5's fixed base has no free-flyer root placement to perturb the way the sibling rigid-body-algorithms leaf's (PR #639) humanoid does). This is the fixed-base analogue of that leaf's nine-number set: with one frozen configuration instead of two and no free-flyer orientation coordinate, five numbers is what the same three categories (independent configuration coordinates, one inertial parameter, one placement number) reduce to. v and a are held at zero, as the upstream example sets them, and are deliberately NOT perturbed: two ulps on an operand that is already exactly zero produces a subnormal number (about 9.9e-324), which every downstream double-precision computation combined with this model's normal-magnitude terms rounds away completely, so perturbing a zero operand would test nothing. The first body's own lever is itself exactly [0, 0, 0] in this model (its inertial origin coincides with the joint frame), so the 'first lever component' entry in this five-number set has the same problem: measured in isolation on the sibling exc-forward-dynamics-derivatives check (same model, same mechanism), its two-ulp move alone produced a bit-identical numerical.jsonl there. It stays in the set, named rather than silently dropped, for the same reason the humanoid siblings keep individually-inert numbers in theirs; the other four numbers already move every non-structural observable of this check. Six of the eight observables are exactly zero in both ic/nominal and ic/variant, for every configuration and every inertial parameter, not only this one, because v=0 and a=0 here (the upstream example's own choice): v_partial_dq (both frames) is the derivative of the joint's spatial velocity with respect to the configuration, and velocity is linear in the joint velocities (v = J(q) qdot), so its q-derivative carries a factor of qdot that is zero; a_partial_dq and a_partial_dv (both frames) are, at qdot=0 and qddot=0, derivatives of terms that are themselves linear or quadratic in qdot and qddot, which vanish identically at that point for any q or any inertial parameter. Only a_partial_da (both frames), the derivative of acceleration with respect to the joint acceleration, is qdot- and qddot-independent (it is the joint Jacobian J(q) itself) and is the sole pair of observables this variant can move. The worst measured spread among those two observables is 1.4433e-15 absolute.
altbuild: none: the same source built at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off reproduces the -O2 result bit-identically for this module, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. Eigen fixes the evaluation order of these expressions and the recursions are scalar, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned source, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead. Measured on the worker (136.114.2.6, x86_64), 2026-09-13, as part of a fourteen-check probe covering the whole leaf.

warrant: The graded quantities are the kinematic derivative blocks of the end-effector joint of a fixed-base UR5 manipulator, in the LOCAL and WORLD frames, dimensionless (the Jacobian blocks) or in SI units, and in the model's own degree-of-freedom order, which is fixed by the frozen model rather than chosen by the implementation; six of the eight are structurally zero at this check's v=0, a=0 setting (see 'variant' above) and are graded as exact-zero identities. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 1.0 (a Jacobian entry), it admits about 1.00e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this test can express is many orders of magnitude larger: a Jacobian column is a recursion over the same spatial algebra as forward kinematics, and dropping a term, transposing a motion subspace or using the wrong reference frame moves individual entries by 1e-2 or more, seven decades above the bound. Measured on this host, injecting a 0.1 per cent error into the largest graded value (a_partial_da_local(4,5), 1.0 to 1.001) is rejected at 9.90e+05 times the bound. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates the recursion differs by about n*eps*|x|, roughly 6 * 2.2e-16 * 1.0, which is 1.3e-15, inside the bound. Measured here: the five-number two-ulp variant moves the worst graded value of the two moving observables (a_partial_da_local, a_partial_da_world) by 1.4433e-15, using 1.437e-06 of the bound, that is 695,795 times of headroom across their 72 graded values. The alternative build measured exactly zero. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault this test is written to catch could pass it.
